rules.sentence: Mucosal melanoma consists of malignant melanocytes of varying phenotypes (epithelioid, spindle-cell, and plasmacytoid) arranged in a sheet-like, organoid, alveolar, solid, or desmoplastic architecture.[96]
Kaposi sarcoma presents with a mixture of vascular slits, extravasated erythrocytes, and proliferating spindle cells.[97]
NHL histopathology shows irregular lymphocytes mixed with plasma cells, histiocytes, and lymphoid follicles.[98]
Mucosal-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) presents with follicle-like structures surrounded by diffuse proliferation of small, round lymphoid cells.[67]
On immunophenotyping, there is a predominant CD20+ B-cells with T-cells positive for CD3+.[98][99]
